definition: Debate and Consensus Patterns is a core concept in Agentic AI. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Debate and Consensus Patterns is
theory.body: Debate and Consensus Patterns describes the methods and patterns used within Agentic AI to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Debate and Consensus Patterns is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Debate and Consensus Patterns matters
theory.body: Without Debate and Consensus Patterns, systems built with Agentic AI are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Debate and Consensus Patterns works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Debate and Consensus Patterns follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Debate and Consensus Patterns.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Debate and Consensus Patterns
theory.body: Debate and Consensus Patterns offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
